newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-LUYT BRANDS ALL BLACKS 'BAD LOSERS'.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-LUYT BRANDS ALL BLACKS 'BAD LOSERS'.

text.p: Louis Luyt, the controversial president of the South African Rugby Football Union (SARFU), has refueled his personal war of words with New Zealand in a rare television interview.
Luyt prompted members of the All Black party to storm out of the 1995 World Cup final banquet after suggesting South Africa, had they competed, would also have triumphed in 1987 and 1991.
"I didn't say anything wrong as far as I'm concerned," Luyt told satellite television viewers in South Africa.

"Dr Craven (SARFU's previous president) first went on record in 1987 saying the All Blacks could not call themselves world champions without the Cavaliers, who were then banned. And in 1991 we were not there either."

The victorious Springboks' late arrival at the dinner and the presentation by Luyt of a watch to Welshman Derek Bevan who had refereed South Africa's contentious semifinal with France also angered guests.
Luyt said: "The Springboks arrived one and half hours late (for the dinner). During that time Colin Meads (the All Black manager) came up to the table and gave me an ear bashing.

"He asked in very strong language where the Springboks were. He said 'we would have been here at seven had we won'. I said, 'Yes, but you didn't win' and he nearly hit me - that made me believe they are really bad losers."

New Zealand's World Cup coach Laurie Mains has since claimed his team were poisoned by a waitress named Susie on the eve of the final which they lost 15-12. Mains said he knew who had paid her to doctor the All Blacks' food but declined to name him.
John Hart, who coached New Zealand to their first series win in South Africa (2-1) last season, also complained his party had been treated with "disdain" by SARFU during their tour.
SARFU strongly denied the charge and accused Hart of whingeing.
